decision_triggers: If line_loss_events is still above zero with the +/-0.05 m span, the loss is not geometric. Check the controller's line_loss handling and the start position before changing geometry again.
If line_loss_events is zero but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, reduce mass to 0.6 kg, since body_width cannot move the off-track limit.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed.
integration_questions: With sensors at +/-0.05 m, do the outer sensors read zero on most of the course? If so, does the controller still steer correctly from the centre sensors?
What weights did you use for the outer sensors, and does the signal stay monotonic across the full span?
Does the summed reading stay above 0.05 on the oval and S-bend at every offset up to the off-track limit?

intent: Widen the seven-sensor array from x = +/-0.03 m to +/-0.05 m, keeping the 16 mm footprint at y = 0.04 m, so that the line stays visible out to about 0.07 m centre offset, beyond the 0.06 m off-track limit. Hold mass, wheel track, wheel radius and body width at their iteration 2 values to isolate the span effect. Expected: line_loss_events at 0 on oval, S-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress above the iteration 2 level on at least one track.
learning: Iterations 1 and 2 showed that footprint alone does not stop line loss. Detection range is set by sensor x plus half the footprint plus half the tape width, so span is the controlling lever. Record whether line_loss_events goes to zero with x_max = 0.05 m. If it does, the loss threshold model is confirmed; if not, the next lever is y position or a controller-side fix.
rationale: Iteration 2 (16 mm footprint, x = -0.03 to +0.03 m) did not remove line loss. The oval and S-bend still each logged one line-loss event, and max_error stayed at 0.0605 to 0.065 m. The footprint change helped the oval's max_error slightly but cut its progress, so the footprint is not the binding lever. The span is. A sensor at lateral position x covers tape while the centre offset is within about 0.0125 + 0.008 = 0.0205 m of x, so with the outer sensors at x = 0.03 m the line is lost once the robot's centre offset passes about 0.0505 m. That is before the 0.06 m off-track limit, which matches the line losses seen on the oval and S-bend. The contract allows sensor x up to +/-0.08 m, so the span can be widened. At x = +/-0.05 m the loss threshold moves to about 0.07 m, beyond the off-track limit, so line loss should be geometrically impossible on the development tracks. Body_width stays at 0.12 m because the off-track limit is fixed at 0.06 m (max(0.06, 0.0125 + bw/4) and bw/4 cannot exceed 0.045 m). Mass (0.7 kg), wheel_radius (0.03 m), wheel_track (0.10 m) and footprint (16 mm) stay fixed so this race isolates the span effect. Expected result: line_loss_events falls to 0 on all tracks, max_error falls below 0.06 m on the oval and S-bend, and completions appear, or at least progress rises. Risk: the outer sensors at x = 0.05 m see no tape at small offsets, so the centre sensors must carry the signal. The Integrator should scale the outer weights to keep the signal monotonic. Rejected alternative: moving y forward again, because iteration 0 showed y = 0.06 m adds lag without fixing the loss.
